source.effective_errata: Issue #518 is attached to §9.7.3 at physical p344/printed p329; its strikeout removes the CMap-side array form of CIDSystemInfo. The effective shape is a dictionary, matching Table 118. Issue #278 on physical p353 is punctuation-only in §9.7.5.3 and does not change Table 118. Table 116/117 rows have no directly applicable EC3 alteration found in the inspected source.

features.source_feature: Table 114 requires ASCII-string Registry and Ordering and an integer Supplement. Registry has a registered-prefix/underscore format; Supplement tracks collection additions. §9.7.3 says compatibility is determined by Registry and Ordering, and explicitly says Supplement shall not be used to determine compatibility. The compatibility rule is a constraint on the PDF's CMap/CIDFont pair.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.7.3 and §9.7.4.1; Table 115 is reviewed separately
features.code: crates/pdf-font/src/composite.rs::collection_names reads Registry and Ordering; it deliberately does not read Supplement. CID mappings use the Type0 CMap and descendant mapping, not a table-114 string validation path.
features.assertion_assessment: The implementation follows the explicit no-Supplement-for-compatibility rule by using only Registry/Ordering where collection identity is needed. The tested CIDs are literal Adobe-Japan1 values. The ASCII/prefix constraints describe producer data; this pass does not infer a reader rejection duty for malformed strings.
features.verdict: No new defect identified. Supplement is correctly absent from the compatibility identity calculation.
features.residuals: No test varies only Supplement through a public rendering path. The post-Table117 version-specific CID ceiling is separately unresolved below; do not conflate that rule with Table114 compatibility.

features.source_feature: Table 116 lists CMap names and their code/CID and horizontal/vertical descriptions. §9.7.5.2 separately says a processor shall support Adobe-CNS1-7, Adobe-GB1-5, Adobe-Japan1-7 and Adobe-KR-9. Identity-H/V map two-byte codes to same-number CIDs, high byte first. The normative names/data are not fully enumerated by a test table copied into source.
features.code: crates/pdf-font/src/predefined.rs holds all 239 Adobe CMap resources (including inherited chains) and constructs Identity-H/V; crates/pdf-font/src/cmap.rs parses mappings/codespaces; crates/pdf-font/src/composite.rs routes Type0 Encoding to predefined CMaps.
features.assertion_assessment: Assertions cover required collection Unicode map data, every carried map's structural usability, a literal Shift-JIS code-to-CID pair, inherited vertical mappings and an exact Type0 public consumer of 90ms-RKSJ-H. ADR 0140 documents the checked-in Adobe source/hash inventory and why it contains all 239 files. These together provide strong but bounded data provenance/consumer evidence.
features.verdict: No map omission or mapping defect identified in this sample. Predefined name and actual Type0 consumer paths are implemented and tested.
features.residuals: The test does not independently enumerate all Table 116 rows or all source map outputs; pinned data hashes and whole-carried-map parser checks provide the current provenance. The version/supplement no-display rule after Table117 remains unresolved and is not certified by these tests.

features.source_feature: Table 117 is intentionally empty to retain numbering. The immediately following §9.7.5.2 prose still imposes support/version behavior: required collection versions are listed, later supplements are cumulative, unsupported newer CMap versions may error, and CIDs added in a supplement later than the processor's supported version are not displayed. Table 117 itself supplies no rows to transcribe.
features.ledger: doc/conformance/ledger.toml §9.7.5.2; current ledger focuses required collection data and identity prohibition
features.code: predefined data includes all carried Adobe CMaps independent of PDF document version; composite::composite_cmap receives the Document but selects a named map without a version/supplement ceiling. Glyph selection then applies the CMap CID to the descendant mapping.
assertions: current global findings 2038-T129 for custom stream inheritance (not version ceiling)
features.assertion_assessment: The current suite tests collection availability and mapped CIDs, but I found no named assertion that checks the explicit newer-supplement no-display rule against the processor's supported version. The implementation path appears version-neutral. However, a valid counterexample requires a source-established CID introduced in a later-than-supported supplement; the held PDF 2.0 table intentionally has no Table 117 data and the shipped Adobe-Japan1 source stops at supplement 7. I did not invent a future collection assignment or claim a runtime conformance failure.
features.verdict: Open evidence gap / bounded residual, not a confirmed defect. Needs authoritative version-to-supplement/CID provenance before a reliable exact-xref regression can be stated.
features.residuals: No drafted test. A future review should source the supported-version supplement ceiling and at least one later-supplement CID from the appropriate normative reference or authoritative collection revision, then check both that code's suppression and an in-version positive control.

features.source_feature: Table 118 keys: Type (required CMap), CMapName (required and equal to CMap file), CIDSystemInfo (required dictionary and same as file except Identity maps need not match), WMode (optional/default 0, integer 0/1 and same as file), UseCMap (optional predefined name or stream; local CMap states differences). §9.7.5.4(a) additionally requires an in-file usecmap base also appear in dictionary UseCMap.
features.code: composite_cmap/read_cmap resolves names/streams, compares WMode, parses mappings and follows UseCMap. If the dictionary entry is absent, it may resolve a carried in-file base directly. It refuses unresolved inheritance; it does not generally enforce identical base names or all producer metadata constraints.
features.assertion_assessment: The prior shard's 'public UseCMap test missing' claim is superseded. Current tracked test and global 2038-T129 use exact xref/no recovery, matching child stream dictionary and in-file base references, exact inherited A→CID/GID36 and override B→CID/GID37, real embedded LiberationSans outlines, and two public display-list glyphs. It passed in font-crypt-controls-wave97 and again in eleven-crate-wave111. Matching metadata and WMode=1 vertical rendering have separate valid public coverage. This is discriminating consumer evidence, not full Table118 malformed-cell certification.
features.verdict: Valid UseCMap inheritance and local override now have strong public evidence. No duplicate test warranted.
features.residuals: No requirement to reject a producer-invalid metadata mismatch is claimed here. Table118's individual invalid-value diagnostics and all CMap operator syntax are outside this bounded pass.

bounded_review: Tables 114, 116, 117, and 118 reviewed; Table 115 is explicitly delegated to the CIDFont dictionary cell shard. No whole-clause certification.
parent_review: T129 remains current PASS evidence; no duplicate test. Processor-supported version is distinct from source document version, so version-neutral lookup alone does not demonstrate a defect. No authoritative later-than-supported CID witness established.
